description: A mirror reflecting earth back to us.
summary: This project is an interactive web mapping website to visualise the 2026 monsoon flooding season along the Jamuna River using NISAR data. The application allows users to drag a split screen comparison  slider and switch between playback and side by side views. This is useful to show the impact of flooding around river basins. NISAR's all weather L band radar penetrates clouds to reveal the floodplain and shifting river morphology and can provide researchers, disaster responders with visual data into the change in river water levels.
details: It is an interactive web mapping application and geospatial pipeline that tracks monsoon flooding and river shifts along Bangladesh's Jamuna river. Using python in Google Colab, I queried NASA's Alaska satellite facility (ASF) for NISAR L-band GCOV radar products, downloaded into Colab and combined the images with Esri open source mapping libraries. Unlike optical satellites blinded by monsoon clouds, NISAR's L-band radar penetrates cloud cover. The impact is to bridge the gap between SAR remote sensing and public understanding of the effect of changes in climate. The tools used were Claude, Google Colab python libraries (asf_search, h5py, array, rioxarray, rasterio, geopandas, numpy), HTML5, CSS3, Vanilla JavaScript, Leaflet.js, Esri World Imagery, OpenStreetMap and Github pages. Originally, the river chosen was the Brahmaputra river, specifically the areas in Kaziranga, but querying the 2026 NISAR GCOV archive across pre-monsoon and monsoon passes showed a problem: the satellite's orbital footprints over Kaziranga did not overlap enough from one date to the next across the target river reach. Some setbacks came from extracting the asf data directly from Colab via login authorisation which yielded errors.
